package_info.why_malicious: These packages were intentionally crafted to exploit dependency confusion, allowing attackers to inject code that exfiltrates sensitive files (e.g., /etc/shadow, .bash_history) and opens reverse shells, providing remote access to compromised systems.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (as soon as the package is loaded or installed)
execution_context.file_location: run.js (main entry point of the malicious package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads the contents of the /etc/shadow file, which contains hashed Linux user passwords.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing /etc/shadow is a clear sign of credential theft, as this file is highly sensitive and should not be accessed by application code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should never access or exfiltrate system password files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administration scripts (run by root) may access /etc/shadow, but never in a third-party dependency.
key_indicators: Use of execSync to run shell commands

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Opens a reverse shell to 5.189.184.129:5482, giving the attacker remote command execution on the victim's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reverse shells are a classic post-exploitation technique, allowing attackers to bypass firewalls and gain interactive access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never open unsolicited network connections or spawn shells.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may use reverse shells, but not production dependencies.
key_indicators: Piping shell I/O to a network socket

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Exfiltrates collected data (username, home directory, current directory, IP addresses, and /etc/shadow contents) to a remote server (comevil.fun) via HTTPS GET request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating sensitive system and credential data to an external domain is a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not send system/user data to unknown external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry in some packages, but never with credential files.
key_indicators: Inclusion of sensitive file contents in request

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads the user's .bash_history file and sends its contents to a remote server controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting .bash_history is a known technique for stealing credentials and sensitive command history.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or exfiltrate shell history files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensics or backup tools may access .bash_history, but not third-party dependencies.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Establishes a POST request to an attacker-controlled ngrok tunnel, used for exfiltrating stolen data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of dynamic tunneling services (ngrok) for data exfiltration is a common attacker tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not communicate with random ngrok endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Temporary development/test tools may use ngrok, but not production dependencies.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed due to dependency confusion (public package name matches internal dependency).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed during package import or installation.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at import-time, harvesting sensitive files (/etc/shadow or .bash_history) and system/user information.
Collected data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled servers via HTTPS or HTTP POST requests.
Reverse shell is established, granting attacker remote access to the compromised system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can execute arbitrary commands on victim machine.

behavioral_signatures: Access to /etc/shadow or .bash_history by NodeJS processes
Outbound network connections to suspicious or dynamic domains (e.g., comevil.fun, ngrok.io)
Spawning of shell processes (e.g., /bin/sh) by NodeJS applications
Unexpected reverse shell activity (NodeJS process connecting to external IP on high port)
file_indicators: Presence of run.js or index.js with credential/file exfiltration logic
References to /etc/shadow or .bash_history in package code
Use of child_process.execSync or spawn in dependency code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for NodeJS processes accessing sensitive files like /etc/shadow or .bash_history, spawning shells, or making outbound connections to known malicious or dynamic endpoints. Use static analysis to flag dependencies containing references to sensitive files or suspicious network destinations. Alert on installation of packages with names matching internal dependencies from public repositories.
